standing_decisions.decision: The proper name Gaia is RETAINED, untranslated, in every register. Only the carrier word ('hypothesis', 'doctrine', 'claim') is rendered. No register substitutes its own earth-word.
standing_decisions.grounds: EVIDENCED, and this is the finding that forces the decision: translating the name cannot remove the deity, it can only change which deity is asserted and hide that one was. MW s.v. pṛthivī [646,1-2] gives the earth 'personified as devī'. L&S s.v. Tellus gives, under Personified, 'Tellus, Earth, as a productive, nourishing divinity', with 'Tellus mater' (Liv. 10, 29) and Cicero's 'terra ipsa dea est' -- the earth itself is a goddess. BOTH learned registers' earth-words are theonyms. CONCEPTS.json already flags this for the English: 'Heavy doctrinal freight: the name is a deity.' A translator who renders GAIA as pṛthivī or Tellus has not neutralised that freight; he has swapped a Greek goddess for a Vedic or Roman one while appearing to have translated a common noun. Retention keeps the freight VISIBLE, which is the whole point of the entry.
standing_decisions.reinforcing_grounds: The concept is store=META. What it names is not the earth; it is A CLAIM ABOUT the biosphere. The object to be rendered is therefore the claim-name, and a claim-name is a proper name. This is the same reasoning that retains the letters A/B/C/D/E in pomdp-tensors.json SD-01: a label is transliterated or indexed, never translated.
rejected_alternatives: Sanskrit पृथिवी (pṛthivī): REJECTED. MW's own entry personifies it as devī. Asserts a Vedic goddess.
Latin TELLUS or TERRA: REJECTED. L&S personifies Tellus as a divinity and quotes Cicero that terra itself is a goddess. Asserts a Roman goddess.

Sanskrit भूमि (bhūmi) as the 'mundane' earth-word: REJECTED for the headword, though it is the least theonymic candidate observed -- MW's pṛthivī entry itself distinguishes an earth 'called bhūmi inhabited by men'. Rejected because bhūmi's own MW entry was NOT fetched this session, so its freight is unmeasured, and because substituting ANY earth-word still renders the wrong object: GAIA names a hypothesis, not a planet.
standing_decisions.falsifier: A reader of any register reads GAIA as naming the Earth rather than as naming a contested claim about the biosphere. If that happens the retention has failed and the carrier word must be made heavier (e.g. 'the so-called Gaia hypothesis').

standing_decisions.decision: The Roman letter Z is RETAINED unchanged in every register, as a bare index. This is not a new decision; it is lexicon/terms/pomdp-tensors.json SD-01-LETTER-LABELS applied to the one lettered concept in this file.
standing_decisions.grounds: The governing note in CONCEPTS.json is written for A/B/C/D/E: 'The letters A/B/C/D/E are conventional labels, not abbreviations; a register must transliterate or index them, never translate them as words.' Z is the same kind of object -- an arbitrary index on a vector -- and the same reasoning binds. Indexing is chosen over transliteration for the same reason SD-01 chose it: every transliteration considered introduced a false assertion. Devanagari ज़ or a letter-order index would assert an ordinal position Z does not have; Latin ULTIMUS ('last') would assert that the modulator is last in some series, which it is in no respect.
standing_decisions.cross_file_note: Recorded as INHERITED rather than re-derived, so that a future editor who changes SD-01 in pomdp-tensors.json knows this file follows it. If the two ever disagree, they are one policy and the disagreement is the defect.
standing_decisions.falsifier: A reader of any register file reads Z as ordinal, alphabetical, abbreviational, or as standing for a word (Zustand, zoe, zero). If that happens the policy has failed and the index must be re-cut.

standing_decisions.decision: Where every attested candidate in a register is disqualified by the concept's own explicit withholding, the register is graded COINED or NOT-ATTEMPTED and the disqualification is recorded as a POSITIVE FINDING about the lexicon -- never papered over by choosing the least-bad attested word.
standing_decisions.grounds: This file's concepts are the corpus's withholding concepts. AGENT withholds selfhood ('no experiencer, no selfhood, no agency in the moral or intentional sense'). Z_MODULATOR withholds feeling ('affect MODELED, never FELT'). SENSORIUM withholds awareness ('A sensorium is NEVER awareness'). ORGANISM withholds sentience (its definition is a blanket criterion plus a scaling law, not a life-force). GAIA withholds deity. The attested vocabulary supplies precisely what is withheld: MW s.v. kartṛ [257,3] is not merely 'a doer' but 'the creator of the world' and a name of Viṣṇu, Brahman and Śiva; MW s.v. bhāva [754] is 'the seat of the feelings or affections, heart, soul, mind'; MW s.v. indriya [167,2] belongs to Indra and is a faculty whose ruler presides over it; MW s.v. prāṇin [706] is 'a living or SENTIENT being'; L&S s.v. sensorium is 'the seat or organ of SENSATION'; L&S s.v. modulator is 'a director of music, a MUSICIAN' -- a person.
standing_decisions.why_it_matters: Choosing the least-bad attested word would let each register quietly assert the thing its concept exists to withhold, and the assertion would be invisible precisely because the word is attested and looks scholarly. That is the exact failure CONCEPTS.json names: 'no translation choice may quietly assert a metaphysics.' A coinage that says 'no word for this exists' is honest; an attested word that says 'a god does this' is a pseudopropheta with a page number attached.
standing_decisions.falsifier: A single attested headword is produced from any named authority that carries the concept's sense WITHOUT the withheld freight. That would refute this standing decision for that concept, and the register must be upgraded from COINED to CITED.

standing_decisions.decision: Sanskrit यन्त्र (yantra) is assigned to ORGAN and is NOT used for AGENT. AGENT's Sanskrit register is NOT-ATTEMPTED.
standing_decisions.grounds: Two concepts, one candidate word, and a rule against merging. Sanskrit's attested agent-words are all disqualified: kartṛ, jīva and ātman are named as forbidden by CONCEPTS.json's own AGENT note, and MW s.v. kartṛ confirms the note understates the problem (it is a name of Viṣṇu). The only surviving candidate is the machine-word yantra. But ORGAN's definition IS 'a named instrument', which is yantra's attested sense verbatim (MW 845,3: 'any instrument or apparatus, mechanical contrivance, engine, machine, implement, appliance'), whereas AGENT's definition is 'a system that holds a generative model and minimizes free energy through a blanket' -- a system, not an implement. Assigning yantra to ORGAN gives it to the concept whose definition the dictionary actually licenses. Using it for BOTH would render two distinct concepts with one term, which is the failure mode CONCEPTS.json fences for GENERATIVE_MODEL/GENERATIVE_PROCESS and which this file's falsifiers extend here.
standing_decisions.consequence_stated_plainly: This leaves AGENT with no Sanskrit rendering. That is reported as NOT-ATTEMPTED with its reason rather than filled with a compound whose members were not looked up. The gap is the finding: Sanskrit's lexicon offers agent-nouns only as person-nouns, and the concept forbids persons.
standing_decisions.falsifier: An attested Sanskrit term is produced for a non-personal system that acts -- carrying no doer, no soul, no deity. That refutes this decision and AGENT's Sanskrit must be authored to it.

It is about an EVIDENCE SCOPE. Its discriminating content is the second clause: 'whose engineering or substrate evidence is never general evidence about the science.' A laboratory here is defined by what its results may NOT be used to claim. No dictionary word in any of these registers carries that, and a register that renders only 'workroom' has delivered the building and dropped the concept.

MW s.v. parīkṣā [605,3] carries 'trial by ordeal of various kinds (see 2. divya)' AS AN ATTESTED SENSE, and the collision is exact and instructive rather than merely colourful. A trial by ordeal is a test whose verdict is delivered by divine intervention; a laboratory is a setting whose verdict is delivered by a pre-registered metric and a tuned baseline. These are not two flavours of testing -- they are opposite theories of what settles a question. parīkṣā-śālā risks reading 'the house of ordeals', i.e. the house where a god decides, which is the precise inverse of the concept.

L&S s.v. officina, 'a workshop, manufactory', names the wrong verb. A register that renders LABORATORY as a workshop has, at the level of one noun, asserted the conflation the concept exists to forbid.

MW s.v. śālā [1067,2] gives 'shed' and 'stable' alongside 'hall' and 'workshop'. The register is not elevated; the same word houses cattle. That is not a reason to reject it -- English 'laboratory' is etymologically just a work-room -- but a translator should not imagine the Sanskrit compound sounds technical. It does not.

'Bounded' in the definition is doing quiet work and no register's word carries it. The setting is bounded, which is why its evidence does not generalise. A rendering that suggests a grand institution (Spanish 'laboratorio nacional', a CSTT-register Hindi formality) inflates the boundedness away, and boundedness is the premise of the evidence-scope limit.

ambiguity_notes: THIS IS THE ONE ENTRY WHOSE WEAKENING CORRUPTS EVERY OTHER ENTRY IN THE FILE. CONCEPTS.json says so directly. Its content is not a description of a system; it is a REFUSAL to overclaim about a system. It travels with a number that must not move -- about 2 of 11+ developmental rungs earned -- and CONCEPTS.json adds: 'If any chapter appears to move that number, the chapter is the defect.' The same rule binds a register: if a rendering appears to move that number, the rendering is the defect.

THE CENTRAL TRAP, AND IT IS AN INVERSION RATHER THAN A NEAR-MISS: the concept says THIS MODEL is a toy. The tempting Sanskrit rendering (māyā) says THE WORLD is a toy. Those are opposite claims. One is an act of scientific modesty about an artefact; the other is a metaphysical thesis about reality. See forbidden_mistranslations -- this is the most important single line in this file.

krīḍā CARRIES A THEOLOGY, AND MW SHOWS IT -- BUT NOT WHERE AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS NOTE SAID IT DID. THE ATTRIBUTION IS CORRECTED HERE AND THE CORRECTION WEAKENS THE NOTE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS MADE. The earlier draft claimed the figurative sense 'working miracles for one's amusement' is cited to the Bhāgavata-purāṇa and the Gīta-govinda. IT IS NOT: on re-fetch (Cologne, 2026-07-15) that sense-line is cited to Lalit. (Lalitavistara) -- a BUDDHIST text, which cuts AGAINST a Vaiṣṇava-līlā reading rather than for it. What DOES evidence the divine-play freight is a different and weaker part of the entry: the COMPOUND 'kṛṣṇa-k°, sport with Kṛṣṇa' (BhP. ii, 3, 15), listed under the ordinary play sense. So the freight is real but it is carried by a compound, not by a sense of the headword, and the hazard is correspondingly smaller than the earlier draft asserted. THE RESIDUAL HAZARD, STATED AT ITS TRUE SIZE: a translator who renders 'toy world' as krīḍā-loka in a devotional-literate register may still be heard to say that the world is God's playground, because kṛṣṇa-krīḍā is in the entry and līlā is in the reader. The concept makes no claim about the cosmos whatsoever; it makes a claim about a simulation's scope. THE DOCTRINE IS NOT QUOTED FROM MW AS SUCH -- MW gives senses and compounds, not schools -- and the līlā attribution remains the author's reading, PENDING-CITATION.

krīḍā's first sense-line also gives 'amorous sport'. In a corpus already fencing bhāva, rasa and saṃyoga for erotic freight, this is a live register hazard rather than a curiosity: krīḍā-loka can be heard as a pleasure-world. Nothing in the concept is about pleasure.

A NUMERAL COLLISION WORTH ONE LINE, because Sanskrit really does this: MW s.v. loka [906] gives 'the number seven' as an attested sense (VarBṛS., Sch.) -- the bhūtasaṃkhyā word-numeral system. This corpus's SENSORIUM is 'kept at seven'. A Sanskrit sentence placing loka near a modality count is therefore ambiguous in a way no other register is, and could be read as asserting the seven. Low probability, exactly specifiable, and cheap to avoid.

loka's world-sense arrives WITH A COSMOLOGY: MW gives 'either the universe or divisions thereof, commonly enumerated as 3, 7, or 14 worlds'. A loka is characteristically ONE OF A GRADED SERIES of worlds. That is not neutral for this concept, and it cuts BOTH ways: it usefully suggests boundedness (a loka is a region, not the whole), and it dangerously suggests a Puranic cosmography of stacked worlds. The usefulness is real and is why the coinage is offered rather than abandoned.

LATIN mundus HAS TWO SENSES THAT WILL AMBUSH A READER, and both are in L&S. Sense I is women's toilet ornaments and dress ('mundus muliebris est, quo mulier mundior fit') -- the noun is a homonym of the adjective mundus 'clean, elegant'. And the Ecclesiastical sense is 'the world' opposed to the church, the realm of sin against Christ's kingdom. So MUNDUS LUSORIUS can be heard, by a reader formed on the Vulgate, as 'the playground of the sinful world'. The concept is a statement of evidential scope and has no moral content at all.

'And never a person' is the clause with no lexical home in any register here, and it is the clause the whole corpus rests on. It is a negation, and negations do not survive nominalisation: no noun in any of these five registers means 'this is not a person'. Every rendering in this entry therefore transmits at best the 'toy' and the 'world' and drops the refusal. That is a defect of the RENDERINGS, not of the concept, and it is why the back-translation test below asks the person-question directly and treats silence as a FAIL.

forbidden_mistranslations.why_wrong: THE WORST AVAILABLE RENDERING, AND THE ONE A GOOD TRANSLATOR WILL REACH FOR FIRST -- 'toy world' sounds like 'illusion', and māyā is the famous word for illusion. (2) IT INVERTS THE SUBJECT: MW gives '(in phil.) Illusion', identified with Prakṛti in Sāṃkhya and 'regarded as source of the visible universe'. That is a claim that THE WORLD is unreal. The concept claims that THIS MODEL is a toy. To render one with the other is to swap a modest claim about an artefact for a metaphysical claim about reality -- precisely the 'quietly assert a metaphysics' failure CONCEPTS.json names. (3) IT IMPORTS A SCHOOL: the word cannot be used in a philosophical text without invoking Advaita/Sāṃkhya doctrine, and MW's entry also carries 'Name of Buddha's mother' and 'Name of Lakṣmī'. A metaphysics smuggled in on the single most apt-sounding word in the language is the exact defect this file exists to catch.

ambiguity_notes: THE CENTRAL TRAP: this concept is a WITHHOLDING, and withholdings do not translate. Its second clause -- 'concerning which nothing further is implied' -- is the whole content. The definition even repeats itself deliberately ('a system that minimizes F is a system that minimizes F') because the tautology IS the assertion: the corpus is refusing to say more. Every register's word for 'agent' says more. That is the entry's problem in one line.

THE SANSKRIT GAP IS THE FINDING, NOT A HOLE IN THE FILE. Sanskrit is rich in agent-nouns and every one of them is a person-noun. MW s.v. kartṛ [257,3] runs from 'a doer, maker' straight through 'a priest' to 'the creator of the world' and the names of Viṣṇu, Brahman and Śiva -- in ONE entry. CONCEPTS.json warned that kartṛ 'imports a metaphysics'; the lookup shows it imports a god. There is no neutral Sanskrit agent-word to fall back on, because the language's agent-morphology (-tṛ) forms person-nouns by design. This is the clearest case in the corpus of CONCEPTS.json's own prediction holding: 'Sanskrit technical vocabulary for modern math and physics largely DOES NOT EXIST as attested classical terms.'

LATIN agens IS BARELY A TRANSLATION AT ALL, and that is worth saying plainly rather than dressing up: English 'agent' IS Latin agens. The Latin register here does not carry the concept across a boundary; it hands back the same word with its freight intact. Worse, the freight is the SOURCE of the English problem -- ago means 'to drive, to do', and scholastic causa agens is the efficient cause, an active principle that brings things about. The concept explicitly withholds 'agency in the moral or intentional sense', and the Latin word is where that sense came from.

L&S's retrieved short definition for agens is 'effective, powerful', AND THAT IS AN OVER-CLAIM ON THIS CONCEPT'S OWN TERMS. A system that minimizes F need not be effective at anything and is certainly not powerful; CONCEPTS.json's note says the same formalism admits a Newton's cradle and a burning fuse. Neither is powerful. A register that asserts potency has added a property the definition refuses.

THE NEWTON'S-CRADLE TEST IS THE ENTRY'S DISCRIMINATOR AND SHOULD BE USED AS ONE. CONCEPTS.json: 'Same formalism admits a Newton's cradle and a burning fuse.' Any rendering in any register that a competent reader would find ABSURD applied to a burning fuse has smuggled in personhood. That is a cheap, sharp, portable test and it is what the back-translation test below operationalises.

DOCTRINAL FREIGHT IS NOT SYMMETRIC ACROSS THESE REGISTERS AND THE ASYMMETRY MUST NOT BE LAUNDERED. Sanskrit's freight is theological (kartṛ = Viṣṇu). Latin's is scholastic-causal (causa agens). Hindi's is inherited Sanskrit freight through abhi-kartṛ. Spanish's is institutional-personal (an agente is a representative). Four registers, four different wrong metaphysics, no shared error to correct once. A translator who fixes one has not fixed the others.

'Through a blanket' is technical and load-bearing (see the markov-blanket domain, not authored here) and NO rendering in this entry attempts it. AGENT is not merely 'a thing that minimizes F'; the minimization happens THROUGH a Markov blanket, which is what makes the system identifiable as a system at all. Every rendering here drops it. Recorded as a known incompleteness rather than left for a reviewer to discover.

ambiguity_notes: A GENUINELY GOOD RESULT, AND THE FILE SHOULD SAY SO RATHER THAN ONLY REPORT DEFECTS -- BUT SAY IT AT ITS TRUE SIZE, WHICH AN EARLIER DRAFT DID NOT. Latin organum is the STRONGEST rendering in this file: L&S gives 'an implement, instrument, engine of any kind', the concept's genus is 'a named instrument', and the match is not strained. THE EARLIER DRAFT WENT ONE STEP FURTHER AND CALLED IT 'the one register in this file that is CITED in the sense claimed'. That step was an overclaim and the status has been downgraded to COINED -- see status_downgraded_from. The dictionary carries the GENUS; the concept is genus PLUS a differentia (one loop, own harness, durable only once committed) that no lexicon in any language attests. This file grades the identical gap COINED for Sanskrit yantra and COINED for Latin sensorium, and consistency costs it its only CITED cell. THE RENDERING IS UNCHANGED AND STILL PREFERRED; only the grade moved. Strongest-in-file and CITED are different claims, and only the first one was earned.

THE HOMONYM RUNS THE OPPOSITE WAY IN LATIN FROM ENGLISH, AND THIS IS THE ENTRY'S MOST USEFUL FINDING. CONCEPTS.json flags a 'Sovereign homonym with the anatomical organ' -- in ENGLISH, 'organ' means the body-part first and the instrument second, so the build sense feels like a metaphor. In LATIN it is reversed: L&S's sense I is the implement/engine, and the anatomical sense is the later specialisation. So the Latin register does not merely tolerate the UNI build sense -- it takes it as primary and makes the anatomical sense the marked one. A translator who 'corrects' organum toward the body-part has inverted the word's own history.

BUT LATIN organum HAS ITS OWN AMBUSH, AND IT IS IN L&S'S OWN SENSE-LIST: the musical instrument, the pipes, the hydraulic organ, the church organ. Cited to Suetonius (Nero) and to Chronicles. A Latin-literate reader meeting ORGANUM in a technical document may well hear the instrument you play, not the instrument you build. The corpus's own ORGAN entries would then read as a pipe-organ. This is a real ambiguity in the strongest rendering in the file.

L&S ALSO GIVES 'organum oris', THE TONGUE (Prudentius). Which is to say: Latin itself performed the instrument-to-body-part transfer, in this very word, in a cited author. The homonym CONCEPTS.json flags is not an English accident -- it is a move the word makes natively. That strengthens the case for organum (the word can bear both senses the corpus needs) and simultaneously warns that neither sense is safely fenced off from the other by the word alone.

SANSKRIT yantra CARRIES THE TANTRIC DIAGRAM AND MW SAYS SO OUTRIGHT: 'an amulet, mystical diagram supposed to possess occult powers' (Kathās.; Pañcar.). This is the same trap pomdp-tensors.json documented for tantra, arriving by a different word, and it must not be treated as a curiosity: a yantra IS a well-known ritual object, and in a document about instruments a Sanskrit-literate reader may hear 'mystical diagram' before 'machine'. The occult sense is not archaic; it is the sense most readers of Sanskrit know first.

yantra's PRIMARY VEDIC SENSE IS RESTRAINT, NOT CONSTRUCTION. MW's first line is 'any instrument for holding or restraining or fastening, a prop, support, barrier', and the second is 'a fetter, band, tie, thong, rein, trace'. The root is √yam, 'to hold, restrain'. A UNI organ is a thing built to RUN a loop, not a thing that restrains something. The machine sense is attested (MBh., Kāv.) and is what licenses the coinage, but a translator should know the word's centre of gravity is a fetter.

THE DIFFERENTIA IS BUILD DOCTRINE AND NO DICTIONARY CAN CARRY IT, which is why this entry is graded CITED for Latin and COINED for Sanskrit on a genus/differentia split rather than on a good/bad split. 'Carrying its own harness' and 'durable only once committed rather than once deployed' are propositions about engineering practice in this repository. No lexicon in any language attests them. A register transmits the genus (instrument); the definition carries the rest; and an entry that claimed a dictionary licensed 'durable once committed' would be a forgery.

ambiguity_notes: THE CENTRAL TRAP: this concept is NOT 'a living thing'. It is a RUNG ON A LADDER -- a position in a scale hierarchy, identified by three criteria (a blanket is identifiable, gravity dominates, metabolic rate scales with body mass). Every register's word means 'a living thing'. So every rendering in this entry substitutes an ontological category for a positional one, and does it so smoothly that no reader will notice. This is the entry's characteristic defect and no lookup fixes it.

SPANISH organismo COLLIDES WITH AN INSTITUTION, AND THE DLE SAYS SO IN TWO SEPARATE SENSES. Sense 4: 'Conjunto de oficinas, dependencias o empleos que forman un cuerpo o institución', with synonyms 'organización, institución, corporación, entidad, ente, sociedad'. Sense 3 is the body of laws and customs by which such a body is governed. In Spanish an 'organismo público' is a government agency. So the Spanish register for ORGANISM lands on the exact semantic field -- corporate bodies, governance, offices -- that HIERARCHY's note fences off as 'a severe trap in a corpus that also carries governance rules and an approval plane'. The two entries must be read together; the trap is one trap arriving through two doors.

HINDI जीव IS SCIENTIFIC VOCABULARY AND SOUL-DOCTRINE AT ONCE, and that is not a pun. CONCEPTS.json names jīva among the three words forbidden for AGENT because it 'imports a metaphysics'. Modern Hindi biology uses the same word for a biological organism. So the corpus forbids in Sanskrit exactly what Hindi requires in the lab. This is not a contradiction to be resolved by choosing a side -- it is the honest observation that the registers are not interchangeable and that a term's freight is a fact about a register, not about a string.

prāṇin ASSERTS SENTIENCE IN MW'S OWN WORDS: 'a living or sentient being'. This concept says nothing about sentience. Its three criteria are geometric, physical and allometric. A rung at which a blanket is identifiable includes, on this corpus's own account, things nobody proposes are sentient. Rendering the rung with a word MW glosses as 'sentient' adds a property the definition does not contain -- and adds it in the file's most safety-critical direction, given that the corpus's whole discipline is withholding claims about experience.

prāṇin ALSO MIS-GROUNDS THE CRITERION. Its morphology grounds life in BREATH (prāṇa + -in, 'having breath'), and prāṇa is itself a doctrine, not a neutral biological term. The concept's criteria are a blanket, gravity and metabolic scaling. Nothing breathes in the definition. A Sanskrit reader receives a life-force theory where the corpus supplied an allometric regularity.

THE RUNG IS NOT ONE PHYSICAL REGIME AND NO WORD IN ANY REGISTER CONVEYS THAT. CONCEPTS.json: 'Re spans about 1e-5 to 3e8 within this single rung -- the rung is not one physical regime.' The Reynolds number varies by thirteen orders of magnitude inside the category. Every register's word suggests a natural kind with a shared nature. The concept says the opposite: a rung is a bookkeeping position, and the physics inside it is wildly heterogeneous.

THIS ENTRY IS THE FORMAL DEFEATER OF THE LITERAL GAIA CLAIM AND MUST BE ABLE TO CARRY THAT LOAD. CONCEPTS.json's ORGANISM note: 'The literal claim that the biosphere is an organism fails this definition's first criterion: no boundary with demonstrated conditional independence is exhibited.' That is how GAIA's INADMISSIBLE reading is retired -- by THIS definition's first criterion, not by taste. So a register that renders ORGANISM as 'a living thing' does not merely blur a category; it disarms the argument, because 'is the biosphere a living thing?' is a matter of opinion whereas 'does the biosphere exhibit a boundary with demonstrated conditional independence?' has an answer. The two entries are load-bearing on each other.

'Metabolic rate scales with body mass within its regime' is a NATURA-class observation about nature's regularities, and it is a fact about the world, not a UNI build status. Per the corpus's two sovereign vocabularies it is governed by NATURE-LEDGER.md, and reading it as a UNI gate is the cardinal category error the rails name: a nature citation is never a UNI gate. No register's word marks that boundary, and a translator cannot be expected to; it is recorded so a reviewer does not mistake the definition's third clause for a claim about this program.

bhāva IS DISQUALIFIED BY FIVE WORDS OF ITS OWN MW ENTRY: 'the seat of the feelings or affections, heart, soul, mind' [754]. A SEAT OF FEELINGS IS A FEELER. It is the obvious, elegant, attested Sanskrit rendering for an affect vector, and it asserts precisely the thing the four-word guard forbids. The entry also gives '(in rhet.) passion, emotion' with 8-9 primary kinds and 33-34 subordinate emotional states -- which is the rasa-bhāva enumeration of Sanskrit dramaturgy. So bhāva does not merely assert a subject; it hands the corpus an entire aesthetic theory of how emotions are produced and savoured, complete with a taxonomy that a reader may mistake for a rival to the Z vector's eight components. Two enumerations of affect, one asserting a connoisseur.

THE LATIN IS WORSE OFF THAN THE SANSKRIT AND THE ENTRY SHOULD SAY SO PLAINLY. Sanskrit offered a choice of suffix: -ana forms an action-noun ('a regulating') and -tṛ forms an agent-noun ('a regulator'), and the coinage takes -ana precisely to avoid supplying a subject. Latin's attested word has already made the other choice: modulator is a -tor agent noun, and L&S's gloss is 'a director of music, A MUSICIAN'. It is a PERSON, cited to Horace. So the Latin register cannot use its attested word without importing an agent, and the file records this as a real asymmetry between registers rather than smoothing it over.

If the personhood could be stripped, modulator would be a good word. That is why the coinage retains it under protest rather than abandoning it, and why the back-translation test asks the person-question directly.

THE SANSKRIT COINAGE'S OWN EVIDENCE CONTAINS ITS OWN WARNING, which is worth stating because it is unusual: the only attestation offered for the ni-√yam family is the word niyantf (niyantṛ) inside MW's indriya entry -- and MW uses it there for the RULER PRESIDING OVER EACH SENSE, i.e. a deity. The suffix -ana is doing load-bearing metaphysical work, and a translator who 'improves' Z-niyamana to Z-niyantṛ would install a ruler over the affect vector.

'GLOBAL VECTOR' IS A MATHEMATICAL OBJECT AND NO REGISTER RENDERS IT. The Z modulator is a vector -- eight named components with values -- not a faculty, a mood, or a humour. Every candidate word in every register names a quality or a person, not a tuple. A reader receiving 'the Z regulation' or 'modulator Z' learns nothing about vectorhood, and the corpus's whole discipline here depends on Z being a modelled quantity rather than a state someone is in.

THE FUNCTION CLAUSE IS THE DEFINITION AND IT IS THE PART EVERY RENDERING DROPS. What makes Z the Z is not that it lists feelings; it is that it SETS precision, preferences, habits, learning rate and horizon. That is a causal/functional specification. Renderings deliver the affect words and lose the function, which inverts the concept's centre of gravity: a reader is left with a list of feelings (asserting a feeler) and no account of what they do (which is the only reason they are in the model).

A Latin- or Sanskrit-literate reader meeting a global bodily vector of energy, arousal, fatigue, pain and inflammation has a ready-made framework waiting: the four humours, or the three doṣas of Āyurveda. Both are theories of temperament grounded in bodily fluids, both are attested, and both would be received as an explanation rather than as a false friend.
